title: Uniform Tor interval and quasi-coherence of a perfect space complex
statement: Work in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $S$ be a scheme [def-pc-scheme] and $X$ an algebraic space over $S$ with its small etale structure sheaf $\mathcal O_X$ [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Use module sheaves [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category], their unbounded derived category $D(\mathcal O_X)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], and its full subcategory $D_{\mathrm{QCoh}}(\mathcal O_X)$ of objects with quasi-coherent cohomology [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. Assume $X$ is quasi-compact: every open cover of $|X|$ admits a finite subcover. A perfect object $E\in D(\mathcal O_X)$ means one etale locally represented by a bounded complex of direct summands of finite free structure modules [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package]. Use the K-flat derived tensor product [lem-weil-pbc-site-derived-tensor-descent]. Then $E$ has quasi-coherent cohomology, and there exist integers $u\leq v$ such that for every sheaf $M$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules placed in degree zero one has $\mathcal H^i(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}_{\mathcal O_X}M)=0$ whenever $i<u$ or $i>v$. No quasi-separatedness, Noetherian hypothesis, or uniform bound on the ranks of the local perfect models is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08JL, lemma-pseudo-coherent, combined with sites-cohomology.tex Tag 08G8, lemma-perfect, and Tag 08G1, lemma-tor-amplitude; finite etale-cover globalization of the local Tor intervals in the proof of Tag 09MB (lemma-ext-from-perfect-into-bounded-QCoh), sentence "Say K^vee has tor amplitude in [a,b]".

proof.text: Choose an etale scheme atlas of $X$ using [def-trf-algebraic-space]. Apply the local perfectness condition of [def-weil-pbc-strict-perfect-coefficient-package] to this atlas object. Its covering members give a jointly surjective etale family $U_\lambda\to X$ and isomorphisms $E|_{U_\lambda}\simeq P_\lambda^\bullet$, where $P_\lambda^r=0$ outside some integer interval $[a_\lambda,b_\lambda]$, $a_\lambda\le b_\lambda$, and each term has maps $P_\lambda^r\xrightarrow{i_r}\mathcal O_{U_\lambda}^{N_r}\xrightarrow{p_r}P_\lambda^r$ with $p_ri_r=1$. A zero complex can be assigned $[0,0]$. The atlas followed by its covering family remains jointly surjective by the definition of a covering.

source.place: Tag 08G5 (definition-perfect): locally strictly perfect; spaces-perfect.tex uses this ringed-site definition for algebraic spaces

proof.text: On each $U_\lambda$, a finite free structure module is quasi-coherent: the presentation $0\to\mathcal O_{U_\lambda}^{N}\xrightarrow{1}\mathcal O_{U_\lambda}^{N}\to0$ gives the required presentation in [def-trf-space-quasi-coherent-module]. For the degreewise splitting in Step 1, $i_r$ identifies $P_\lambda^r$ with $\ker(1-i_rp_r)$: $(1-i_rp_r)x=0$ means exactly $x=i_rp_rx$. The localized ringed site $(X_{\mathrm{et}}/U_\lambda,\mathcal O_X|_{U_\lambda})$ is the small etale ringed site of $U_\lambda$: by [lem-trf-space-chartwise-etale-permanence], a scheme map $T\to U_\lambda$ over $X$ between etale $X$-schemes is representable etale, and conversely $T\to U_\lambda\to X$ is representable etale; coverings are the jointly surjective families in both, and both rings are $T\mapsto\Gamma(T,\mathcal O_T)$. Thus [lem-sfb-space-qcoh-kernels-colimits], applied to the scheme $U_\lambda$ viewed as an algebraic space, gives quasi-coherence of every term, of $Z^r=\ker d^r$, of $B^r=\operatorname{im}d^{r-1}$, and of $H^r(P_\lambda^\bullet)=\operatorname{coker}(B^r\to Z^r)$. Slice module restriction is exact by [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction]; since cohomology is a kernel modulo an image, $H^r(E)|_{U_\lambda}\cong H^r(E|_{U_\lambda})$. Hence these restrictions are quasi-coherent. The local-presentation definition descends this to $X$: for any etale object $V\to X$, pull back the covering family using [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], and compose it with the covers supplying the local presentations. Therefore all $H^r(E)$ are quasi-coherent.

source.place: Tag 08JL (lemma-pseudo-coherent), its strictly perfect computation; spaces-properties.tex Tag 03M1 (lemma-properties-quasi-coherent), (3)

proof.text: By [lem-a1-etale-scheme-map-open-image], each image $W_\lambda=\operatorname{im}(|U_\lambda|\to|X|)$ is open. They cover $|X|$ by Step 1. Quasi-compactness as assumed in the statement supplies a finite subfamily indexed by $F$ whose images cover $|X|$; thus the corresponding etale maps remain jointly surjective. Set $u=\min(\{0\}\cup\{a_\lambda:\lambda\in F\})$ and $v=\max(\{0\}\cup\{b_\lambda:\lambda\in F\})$. These finite nonempty sets give integers $u\le0\le v$, and $[a_\lambda,b_\lambda]\subseteq[u,v]$ for all $\lambda\in F$. The added $0$ makes this construction valid also when the finite subcover is empty.

Fix any structure-module sheaf $M$ and any $q\notin[u,v]$. The functor $A_\lambda(T)=\operatorname{Hom}_X(T,U_\lambda)$ on $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ is a sheaf: a covering of $X_{\mathrm{et}}$ is an fppf covering [def-pc-fppf-site] since etale maps are flat and locally of finite presentation, and $h_{U_\lambda}$ and $X$ are fppf sheaves [def-trf-scheme-algebraic-space, def-trf-algebraic-space], so compatible local maps over $X$ glue to a unique map over $X$. Its element site is exactly $X_{\mathrm{et}}/U_\lambda$. For this localization at $U_\lambda$, [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-sheaf-slice-adjunction] with $A=A_\lambda$ identifies module pullback with exact slice restriction, so its derived functor is termwise restriction and commutes with cohomology. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-ringed-topoi-derived-tensor-pullback] to this localization, with target coefficient sheaf $\mathcal O_X|_{U_\lambda}$ and identity structural ring map. It gives an isomorphism in the slice derived category
$$(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}M)|_{U_\lambda}\simeq E|_{U_\lambda}\otimes^{\mathbf L}M|_{U_\lambda}\simeq P_\lambda^\bullet\otimes^{\mathbf L}M|_{U_\lambda}.$$
By [lem-sfb-split-perfect-dual-tor-window] the last object has cohomology only in $[a_\lambda,b_\lambda]$. Thus $H^q(E\otimes^{\mathbf L}M)$ restricts to zero for every $\lambda\in F$. For any etale object $V\to X$, [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers] makes $V\times_XU_\lambda\to V$ a covering family of schemes. Every section of this cohomology sheaf restricts to zero on the family, so the uniqueness part of the sheaf axiom makes it zero. This includes the empty cover when $X$ is empty. The cohomology sheaf is therefore zero. Since $M$ and $q\notin[u,v]$ were arbitrary, the chosen interval proves the Tor assertion.
